scope: Independent exact revised-pixel review; original parable-art-review-29.json remains unchanged. No import or page edits.

entries.alt: A gray-bearded steward holds one small coin above the empty open palm of a worker in russet, while a bald worker in blue holds his own coin nearby.
entries.caption: The steward pays the workers at evening, beginning with those hired last. When the early workers receive the same wage, their expectation of more brings the owner's generosity into question.
findings: Inspected exact new original at full resolution. The former pale oval suggesting a coin already received is removed; the receiving hand now reads as empty, with skin/finger highlights rather than a separate silver disk. One incoming coin remains pinched above it.
The bald late worker retains one coin. Extra coins remain in the wage box, not in the early receiving hand. No exact inscription or coin denomination is claimed from pixels.

Working continuity preserved: russet early worker, older headwrapped worker, bald blue late worker and youthful gray late worker remain distinct and consistent with01/02. Green-clad gray-bearded steward remains distinct from clean-shaven ochre owner.
Receiving fingers, steward pinch grip, purse grip and late worker palm remain anatomically coherent after correction. No extra hands or fused coin contacts identified.
Purposeful gaze and restrained early-worker disappointment remain; photorealistic faces, cloth and evening light retain the original mood.
Matthew20:8-10 supports evening payment by steward, last hired paid first and equal wage. Scene details are artistic depiction within the parable; no Christ likeness or new historical claim.
conditions: Use source-grounded caption; do not claim the coin inscriptions or exact archaeological setting are verified.
